messages:
lina: quick design check — sharing the compact regression-diff list mock. can people scan for keyboard focus, copy clarity on CTAs, and a11y nits? screenshot: https://img.redwood.local/ux/compact-diff-2024.png design-bot: uploaded image (compact-diff-2024.png) :framed_picture: devin: a11y first pass — when tabbing from the left checkbox the next focus lands on the diff actions (⋯) instead of the diff title. seems like DOM order = actions then content. reproducer: tab to item, press space to expand, focus should move into the expanded panel but it stays on the action button. asif: copy nit — primary bulk CTA reads "Approve selected" which reads like approving the prompt set rather than the eval results. suggestion options: "Approve tests", "Mark as passed", or "Publish approvals". prefer single-action clarity. maia: +1 to copy change. also we need a clear undo path for bulk approves. keyboard users need an aria-live toast with an Undo button that is tabbable. devin: proto idea for the toast: ```html
3 tests approved.
``` this keeps screen readers informed and gives keyboard focus to the undo button if user presses shift+tab after the toast appears. lina: accessibility contrast note — primary CTA (#0a72ff currently) measures ~3.9:1 on the mock. needs to be >=4.5:1 for AA small text or change to a filled style for emphasis. can we try #005ec8 or add a 2px outline? asif: on the CTA label — also consider consistency with other console flows. our rollout approval in dedicated UI uses "Confirm and approve". maybe keep verbs consistent to avoid confusion. maia: keyboard behavior edgecase — when you're typing a comment in the eval sidebar, mod+enter currently submits the parent approval action too because global shortcuts are active. we should scope global shortcuts when a text input has focus. devin: good catch. will add an internal note: `shortcut-manager: ignore global shortcuts when input[aria-multiline]=true` lina: microcopy question: bulk confirm pattern — should we require typing a confirmation token (e.g., "CONFIRM") or a simpler checkbox? typing is safer but slower for PMs doing lots of small approvals. thoughts? asif: prefer checkbox + stronger toast + audit log entry. typing token reserved for destructive ops (delete data). approvals are reversible with undo and audit trail so checkbox is enough. maia: agree with checkbox. also request that the checkbox is focusable first in the confirm dialog so screen reader users don't miss it. devin: implementation detail: make confirm dialog trap focus, place checkbox first, then the CTA. Add `aria-describedby` on the CTA pointing to the small help text explaining undo window (30s). lina: perfect. i'll update the mock and push a small variant that raises contrast + moves DOM order to content->actions. will also change CTA to "Approve tests" and add toast with Undo + aria-live. lina: assigning followups: @devin for focus/shortcut changes, @asif for final CTA copy, @maia for QA accessibility checklist. will share updated figma link later tonight. thanks :thumbsup: devin: ack, I'll add a testing checklist to the PR and log the shortcut fix. asif: I'll run copy through content style and ping back with two variants. maia: i'll run keyboard + screen reader sweep on staging once the PR lands. :a11y:
